notes.title: The Sirena Expedition is coming to Nintendo Switch!
notes.content:
Hello,

I'm excited to announce that [url=https://www.sirenaexpedition.com/]The Sirena Expedition[/url] is coming to Nintendo Switch on the 16th of August 2024! The port has been handled by Ant Workshop (makers of Dungeon Golf and the upcoming Into the Restless Ruins), and I can confirm they've done a great job of it. You can pre-order the game in the following regions:

[list]
[*] North America: [url=https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/the-sirena-expedition-switch/]https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/the-sirena-expedition-switch/[/url]
[*] Europe: [url=https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Nintendo-Switch-download-software/The-Sirena-Expedition-2608616.html]https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Nintendo-Switch-download-software/The-Sirena-Expedition-2608616.html[/url]
[*] Australia: [url=https://ec.nintendo.com/AU/en/titles/70010000083376]https://ec.nintendo.com/AU/en/titles/70010000083376[/url]
[/list]

If you haven't already bought the game, or you know someone who was interested but unable to play it on Steam, now's the perfect chance! And to coincide with the launch, the game will be 20% off on Steam for a week from the 16th of August.

See you at the bottom of the ocean!

notes.title: The Sirena Expedition v1.12 is now live!
notes.content:
Hello there! It's been a while, but I've got an update which includes some bug fixes, and also a bit of news. First, the patch notes:

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where you could pull a block backwards into a wall, and the block would slowly clip into you.
[*] Made some changes to the movement code when going down slopes, so it's hopefully a bit smoother.
[*] Fixed a bug where jumping as soon as exiting a ladder at the top or bottom could cause you not animate correctly.
[*] A couple of tweaks to camera angles in two places, so that things are highlighted better.
[/list]

So, with that out of the way, I'd also like to announce that; a) The game will be on sale at 50% off as part of the Steam Summer Sale, starting on the 27th of June, and b) The Sirena Expedition is coming to Nintendo Switch on the 16th of August! I'm very excited about the port, which has been handled by Ant Workshop (who also ported Thomas Was Alone and Lair of the Clockwork God).

Thanks again for your continued support!

notes.title: The Sirena Expedition v1.11 is now live!
notes.content:
Okay, so I know I said the game was finished, but I received a report for a progression-stopping bug, so I spent a couple of days fixing that. Here are the details:

[list]
[*] Fixed a number of issues with ultra-widescreen aspect ratios (wider than 16:9). There were two points in the game where you couldn't progress because the camera didn't frame your character correctly, and a number of others where it wasn't clear what you needed to do because things were offscreen.
[*] Also fixed a potential soft-lock at standard aspect ratios in the second playthrough, where you could teleport to a block and then not be able to teleport back to it.
[/list]

That's basically it! Nice and straightforward this time. Now, back to work on finalising the soundtrack.

notes.title: The Sirena Expedition v1.10 is now live!
notes.content:
Well, here it is! Finally, I've updated the game with all of the last pieces of music. There's about 15 minutes of new music, on top of the ~24 minutes that was there already, so I'm quite happy to have this in the game. Here's the full change log:

[list]
[*] Added new music to the game, and updated all existing music to be mixed and mastered slightly better.
[*] Moved a couple of pieces of music on the Rooftop around so that they triggered in slightly different places.
[*] Fixed an issue where attempting to teleport from non-flat ground would often give you a message saving you needed more space around you, instead of telling you you can only teleport from flat ground.
[/list]

I believe this is everything! I'm excited for everyone to hear the new music, and will hopefully be releasing a soundtrack soon. If you haven't bought the Sirena Expedition yet, I will be putting it on sale on the 26th of February, so you might want to wait until then to pick it up!

Thanks again to everyone who's bought and played the game so far! I'll post another update once the soundtrack is available, but otherwise, I think the game is (finally) done!

Kind regards,
Giraffe Cat.

notes.title: The Sirena Expedition v1.09 is now live!
notes.content:
Hello again! This, by my reckoning, will be the second last update to The Sirena Expedition. I'm currently working on the final bits of music, which I did want to get into this build, but I'm going to be showing the game at [url=https://www.teamdebug.com/u]Debug U[/url] tomorrow and I wanted to get a couple of features in. These are:

[list]
[*] I implemented new title screen cameras for when you have completed the game at least once.
[*] I changed the way the save system works a little. Without wanting to get into the weeds too much, the way it previously worked was if you saved the game while dialogue was playing, it would put you back to where you were when the dialogue started; however, if you triggered multiple pieces of dialogue before the previous one finished, they would get queued up, and if you saved the game before the last piece of dialogue in the queue played, you would again go back to where you were when the first dialogue started. This could lead to you having to redo up to a minute of gameplay, which I never really liked. The way this system now works is that save states also get queued along with dialogue, so you always save where you were when the current piece of dialogue was triggered (which might not necessarily be the same as when it started playing). It seems like a small thing, but it required quite a big reworking of the logic behind this system.
[*] Fixed a few minor bugs.
[/list]

And that's it! I've got about half of the new music done already, and I'm excited to see how it sounds in-game. With any luck, the next (and final) update will go live some time next week. See you then!

notes.title: The Sirena Expedition v1.08 is now live!
notes.content:
Hello! It's been a while, but I've just pushed a new update. The major addition this time is a checkpoint system, and there are a few more bug fixes, as detailed below.

[list]
[*] The new Checkpoint system creates checkpoints based on your game state at 6 points in the game. This is intended to be a fallback in the case that you lose progress due to a bug or forgetting to save, as well as allowing you to explore earlier parts of the game a bit easier once you've completed it.
[*] The Checkpoint system will also create any checkpoints you havent passed through; this will only be relevant if you already have a save game prior to v1.08's release. If you do, you can load it up and continue playing, and once you reach the next relevant checkpoint, that will be created based on the current game state, whereas all prior checkpoints will be created with a generic game state. If you have already completed the game, and have a save game from that, loading it up and then exiting will be enough to create all six checkpoints.
[*] Fixed the ridiculous issue where the bubbles on the Bathysphere at the start of the game would only play once, and if you started the game again you wouldn't get any bubbles.
[*] Fixed the issue where certain bits of audio (mainly on horror events) weren't being affected by the sound effects volume, so they would be a lot louder than other sounds.
[*] Made the sound effects for the eye that appears on the wall in one of the corridors much less abrasive.
[*] A couple of other minor bug fixes.
[/list]

Thanks again for your support! I've got maybe one or two updates before I'm calling the game done (outside of bug-fixes for any issues that might come up).

notes.title: The Sirena Expedition v1.07 is now live!
notes.content:
Hello! I've just updated the build with a few more bug fixes and QoL improvements. Here are the main things:

- I fixed a number of potential soft-locks and sequence breaks to do with teleporting to blocks you shouldn't be able to teleport to, or not being able to teleport back to blocks you just teleported to.
- Fixed an issue some players were getting where the footstep sounds would play rapidly when going down slopes or stairs. This was actually caused by the fact that while the Option menu was reporting the FPS as 120 by default, it was actually being set to unlocked. Because my slope-handling code is a bit weird and framerate-dependent, you could get stuck on tiny changes in height at high enough framerates, and going down slopes it would think you were continually walking off a ledge and landing, hence the footstep spamming.
- Even though neither of the above issues occur at 120fps, I've put a fix in for them anyway, just in case.
- I also noticed that it was possible to get stuck in one particular wall at the start of the Abyss section. Again, this was framerate-dependent, but I've fixed it. I've also made the game check whether you're inside collision when loading a save, and if you are it should find a safe space for you.
- I put a second switch to open the door at the top of the Abyss, because it was possible (albeit fairly illogical) to close it after you'd pulled the block out, and then use the block to jump over the door and get stuck on the other side.
- Added some secret things.

With that, I'm most of the way towards getting everything I wanted into the game. I've got a few more features I want to implement (a checkpoint system, and a different title screen for when you complete the game), and a few more bug fixes (plus whatever else I find in the meantime), but that's pretty much it! Thanks for sticking with me over the past month and a bit. I realise that the game was a bit messy when it launched, but I'm happy with how far it's come.

notes.title: The Sirena Expedition v1.05 is live!
notes.content:
Hello! It's been a while; I've been working on a pretty big update, but for a lot of players, this won't be much different from the previous build.

- All of the post-game content is finalised now. It's hard to say much about this without spoiling things, but whereas the post-game content before was largely the same as the main game, there are a number of key differences now. Feel free to reach out to me if you'd like more of an explanation!
- If you do already have a post-game save, the game will check whether it's still valid. Because so much has changed, there's potential for your old save to be broken. If the game detects that it won't work at all, it will make you start a new game; in other cases it will advise you to start a new game, but you have the option to continue with your old save if you want to. I don't advise this, because there is the potential for things to be in the wrong place. I can only apologise if you lose progress because of this, but I couldn't think of any way around it.
- I fixed a few bugs where some players would get stuck on bits of scenery, and also hopefully the bug that some players had where walking down stairs would rapidly play footstep sounds.

That's all for this release. I should have an update that adds achievement support pretty soon. I've been tracking achievements in the game itself since launch, but the Steam integration wasn't finished. Once I do that, the first time you boot the next build of the game up, it will check to see what you've unlocked, and retroactively give you those achievements. In theory, anyway!

notes.title: The Sirena Expedition v1.04 is live!
notes.content:
Me again! I've got a new build today, with a fix and a new feature:

- Fixed the issue where attempting to use your special power repeatedly in an area where you can't use it would cause the Aquanaut to lock up.
- Added an accessibility menu to the Options Screen. The only option currently is to turn the pixellation off, as some players might struggle with this.

If anyone has any ideas for other things they'd like to see in the accessibility menu, feel free to let me know, and I'll see how easy they are to implement.

Cheers!

notes.title: The Sirena Expedition v1.03 is live!
notes.content:
Hello! There's a new build of the game available now. This fixes a major progression blocker that a few people were getting, along with a few smaller QoL fixes:

- Fixed the issue where some people were unable to jump up to a certain walkway in one of the puzzle rooms (shortly after you get your new power).
- Made the way the game handles slopes and ledges more consistent across all framerates; previously lower framerates would cause you to pop up onto ledges that you couldn't reach at higher framerates, but this is no longer the case. In my testing, all ledges in the game were reachable, but let me know if anything isn't for you, and I'll fix it.
- Title screen music now continues playing after starting a game.
- Changed how the end of the game deals with saving. Previously it was possible to save in the very last section, but now I've made it so that if you save here, it puts you back at a point where you can go back and look for secrets. Your save game is no longer cleared when you complete the game, so you don't have to start from the beginning again.

Thanks to everyone who's played the game so far, and to everyone who's reported issues!

notes.title: The Sirena Expedition v1.02 is live!
notes.content:
Hello! I've just uploaded a new build that fixes the following issues:

- A lot of the music in the second half of the game wasn't playing. It does now!
- There were some pretty nasty game-state bugs that were caused by saving the game, returning to the title screen and starting again from the beginning (Specifically to do with getting teleported to the abyss, which would generally break the game). I'm fairly sure this is fixed now, but I'll be keeping an eye on it.

Thanks to everyone who's played so far, and sorry for any issues you might have had!
